coverage_note: Order-matters recap, the permutation-with-repetition template n^k and one example (8!/(5!3!) = 56) were readable. The binomial theorem, Pascal's identity and Vandermonde were past the cut.
concepts: Permutation = order matters; combination = order does not.
Permutation with repetition is just the product rule over positions: n^k.
In English word/string questions repetition is allowed by default.
8!/(5!3!) = C(8,5) = 56 for arranging 5 identical stars and 3 identical bars.
